episodes.201329: Several supercell thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a stalled front draped over the Mid-Atlantic. One of these thunderstorms produced a waterspout over the lower tidal Potomac River.
episodes.201330: Scattered showers and thunderstorms in northwest flow produced numerous instances of gale-force winds.
episodes.201338: Scattered severe thunderstorms (a mix of lines and supercells) produced large hail, damaging wind gusts, and tornadoes in the vicinity of a front draped across the Mid-Atlantic.
episodes.201339: Scattered thunderstorms in northwest flow produced several instances of wind damage.
episodes.201340: Scattered thunderstorms in northwest flow produced several instances of wind damage.
episodes.201341: Scattered thunderstorms in northwest flow produced several instances of wind damage.
episodes.201354: A trough over the Mid-Atlantic region pushed a cold front south into the central North Carolina region during the evening hours. Isolated storms became more numerous over the Triangle region, leading to a swath of damaging wind reports over Wake and Johnston Counties.
episodes.201413: A warm front lifted into the area on the night of May 29th and remained present overhead until being ushered east by a low the evening of the 30th. Behind this system, a cold front approached from the north and slowly descended southward through the Ohio Valley on the 31st.||Rounds of rain moved across the area on the 30th, with some additional showers lingering overnight. Around an inch of rain fell across southeast Ohio during this time. Soils had become increasingly saturated during rounds of rain in addition to storms that occurred earlier in the month. Thus, even somewhat lesser rainfall amounts were enough to cause flash flooding across portions of Gallia, Meigs, Lawrence, and Washington counties.
episodes.201414: A warm front lifted into the vicinity of West Virginia on the night of May 29th and remained present overhead until being ushered east by a low the evening of the 30th. Behind this system, a cold front approached from the north and slowly descended southward through the area on the 31st.||Rounds of rain and storms moved across the area on the 30th, with several severe thunderstorms downing power lines and numerous trees during the afternoon. While the majority of precipitation tapered off by the morning of the 31st, a few additional showers sprouted up in parts of southeastern West Virginia during the afternoon. ||The bulk of the area received less than an inch of rain, though some parts of northern, southwest and southeast West Virginia accrued up to around 2 inches. Soils had become increasingly saturated during subsequent rounds of rain and storms earlier in the month; thus, even somewhat lesser rainfall amounts were enough to cause flooding across portions of Doddridge, Harrison, Mason, Tyler, and Wood Counties.
episodes.201545: Thunderstorms developed over the central portion of the 2022 Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar in the early afternoon of May 31st. One of these storms produced heavy rain over upper portions of the Gallinas and Sapello Rivers. An estimated 1 to 2 inches of rainfall produced flash flooding within these drainages that overtopped low water crossings that reached down the Gallinas Creek to areas between Montezuma and Las Vegas.||Key Word: Burn Scar Flash Flooding.
episodes.201577: A cluster of thunderstorms developed and moved through Eastern NC during the early evening. One particular storm became severe and produced wind damage in Craven County.
episodes.201615: A warm front lifted north across the waters of Eastern North Carolina bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms to the Coastal waters of North Carolina on the evening of the twenty-ninth. A few isolated thunderstorms became strong to severe in nature bringing strong and damaging winds to the Coastal waters of the Crystal Coast up to Cape Hatteras.
episodes.201767: Showers and thunderstorms developed along a slow moving cold front and produced a quick one to locally three inches of rain in a short period of time.
episodes.201860: On May 31, 2025, a compact shortwave trough dove south across the Plains. In response, isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across eastern Nebraska during the afternoon and evening, supported by SBCAPE values ranging from 1000 to 1500 J/kg and modest ascent associated with the approaching wave.||Although the environment lacked strong low-level forcing and sufficient wind shear to support organized or long-lived storms, a thunderstorm in Lancaster County managed to produce hail estimated up to 1 inch in diameter. Thunderstorm activity gradually diminished through the evening hours.
episodes.202539: Early thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.202817: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms formed in the afternoon and evening hours of May 30 ahead of a strong cold front. A nearby warm front and enhanced low-level wind shear also allowed for the development of a few supercell thunderstorms.
episodes.202975: Thunderstorms, in the vicinity a cold front, produced flash flooding.
episodes.202976: Thunderstorms, in the vicinity a cold front, produced flash flooding.
episodes.202998: Strong thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front across southeast Georgia in the afternoon hours. These storms then moved out across the Atlantic coastal waters and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.203091: Surface low pressure tracked across northern West Virginia on May 30th. Some instances of wind damage were noted, especially due to saturated ground and wind generally in the range of 30 to 40 MPH.  However, flash flooding had the higher impact, especially in Marion and Monongalia Counties, as 2 to 3.5 inches of rain fell on ground that was already saturated. Widespread flooding of roads, creeks, and streams was reported, with one water rescue noted and several debris flow incidents.
episodes.203176: An intensifying coastal low pressure system brought prolonged moderate to locally heavy rainfall beginning early Saturday, May 31 through that same afternoon before lightening and gradually tapering off in the evening and into the overnight. Rainfall totals across eastern New York ranged from around one inch to three and a half inches with a maximum total of 3.95 inches in Ulster County. A couple of reports of poor drainage flooding were relayed to NWS Albany with the most significant impact being the closure of NY295 going both directions between Rod and Gun Club Road and Hartigan Road in Chatham in Columbia County. Additionally, the combination of strong synoptic winds and very moist soils led to a handful of reports of downed trees and wires, specifically in Dutchess County.
episodes.203340: A line of thunderstorms produced gusty winds across the Chesapeake Bay during the evening hours of May 30 ahead of a strong cold front.
episodes.203341: A broad trough and cold front over the Mid-Atlantic led to the development of strong to severe thunderstorms across the lower Maryland Eastern Shore on the afternoon of May 31. These storms mainly produced large hail, although a few sub-severe wind gusts were also reported.
episodes.203342: A broad trough and cold front over the Mid-Atlantic led to the development of scattered thunderstorms across eastern Virginia on the afternoon and evening of May 31. These storms produced isolated instances of large hail.
episodes.203344: Scattered thunderstorms moved across the Virginia and Maryland coastal waters, lower James River, and Chesapeake Bay in the afternoon and evening of May 31. These storms produced gusty winds.
episodes.203552: Severe thunderstorms developed just ahead of a cold front progressing southward through the region.
episodes.203554: Severe thunderstorms developed just ahead of a cold front progressing southward through the region.
episodes.203559: Waterspouts observed off of Anna Maria Island and Casey Key with morning and evening offshore convection, respectively.
episodes.203560: Morning thunderstorms with a mesoscale convective system associated with a cold front moving across the peninsula produce a lightning strike to a home near Clearwater in Pinellas County.
episodes.203564: Morning thunderstorms with a mesoscale convective system associated with a cold front moving across the peninsula produce gusty marine winds across West Central Florida waters.
episodes.203566: Strong low pressure system brought widespread soaking rains to  the region, with most areas total rainfall amounts generally 1-1.25,  with locally higher amounts in southern and central New Hampshire. A pivot point of the storm system occurred between Milford and Contoocook, resulting in rainfall amounts between 2 to 4 inches. This caused a handful of road closures due to flooding as antecedent rainfall over the past month allowed for saturated soils.
episodes.203705: A mid-level trough over Florida and a weak frontal boundary contributed to the development of strong thunderstorms which moving over the SE Florida coastline, producing hazardous wind gusts in the Atlantic coastal waters.
episodes.204336: River flooding was observed along the White River.
